claim: the walk does the five steps in this order
fix: "The step is a tree walk from the root instance. At each component: 1. it is collected by path; 2. its class is read off declaration shape (§8.5); 3. a primitive's contracts are collected: `u_types`, `y_types`, `*_init` values, `state_events`. At each assembly, after its children: 4. its boundary declarations are evaluated, recording the input and output faces it declares; 5. its wires are resolved to absolute primitive terminals, each face's route recorded beside it. Face derivation and wiring resolution thus run together, bottom-up."
ver_evidence: src/structure.jl:538-571: a primitive is collected, classified and its contracts read during the visit. At an assembly (src/structure.jl:575-700) the children are walked first. Then each level's boundary declarations are evaluated (623) and its local, input and output wires are resolved to primitive terminals (627 onward) in the same visit, before the parent's. Face derivation and resolution are not separate steps, and resolution is not a later global pass. Only the obligation check (452) runs after the walk.

claim: abstract entries only occur on component-fed inputs
fix: Abstract entries occur only on component-fed inputs, which the probe sources from upstream products, and on a root input's abstract co-consumers, which receive the value synthesized at its one concrete declaration ([§8.2][s8-2], [D-236][d-236]).
ver_evidence: src/build.jl:916-933: a root input takes its type from the one concrete consumer entry, and abstract co-consumers are admitted under the bound clause. Probe: Group(n = Negator(), a = AbsIn() with u_types (u = Real,)), input_wires ('in' => ('n/u', 'a/u')) builds with root type Float64. The abstract entry `Real` on a/u is fed by the root input, not by a component. Synthesis still meets only the concrete type.
ver_note: D-236 (abstract co-consumers checked by the bound clause) and spec §8.2 at spec.md:3123-3124 record the fan-out rule.

claim: everything the probe writes is garbage once the build finishes
fix: At init! of a Model at a non-nominal scalar, establish the frozen discrete cells from a nominal establishment round, as the services' seeded half does (D-213), so no probe product is ever read as a value after the build.
ver_evidence: src/build.jl:561-567: the Activation cached on the Build keeps the complete probe products. src/build.jl:1502-1516 compile writes them, and the synthesized root-input values, into every Model's table as its pre-init content. src/model.jl:691-694: at a non-Float64 Model, a frozen discrete component's pinned cells 'keep the carried nominal products — at boundary zero as everywhere'. So probe products outlive the build, and a standalone Model{Dual} run reads them as values. D-213 fixed this only for trim's and linearize's scratch worlds (_establish_frozen!, model.jl:148-160).
ver_note: At Float64, boundary zero overwrites every seeded cell (D-205), and init!'s totality check covers the root inputs, so the leak is limited to frozen cells at a Dual activation. A doc-side alternative would say that the probe's products seed each table until boundary zero writes them.

claim: after pre-materialization the shared Build is fully immutable with no synchronization on any path
fix: Pre-materialize the activations the sweep will need. The shared `Build` then derives nothing at run time, and each lookup takes the build's lock only briefly, at service time and never on the hot path.
ver_evidence: src/build.jl:970 takes build.lock on every lookup, a hit included; src/model.jl:121 calls activation() at each Model construction, so a pre-materialized build still synchronizes on that path

claim: A cell address is a build-time offset carried in an entry field with the port type as its parameter
fix: A cell address is a build-time offset into each block its leaves occupy, one per element type, so a mixed-leaf cell spans several blocks. The offsets are carried in an entry *field*, with the port type as the address's own parameter.
ver_evidence: src/store.jl:11-13 `struct CellAddr{P,K}; offsets::NTuple{K,Int}` has one offset per distinct leaf eltype. src/build.jl:433-434 builds it with `length(eltypes)` offsets. Probe P2: MixedCell's port address is `CellAddr{TaggedValue{Float64},2}` with offsets (0, 0), across the Float64 and Int blocks. test/test_store.jl:56-61 does the same. Field carriage and the port-type parameter match: executor.jl:56-60, store.jl:11.
ver_note: The spec never says that a cell can span several element-type blocks. The store.jl:1-9 comment cites a 2026-08-20 'C2M' bench that appears in no spec or log text. D-162's Position says 'build-time offsets' in the plural, which fits either reading.
